skill.name: spawn-agent
skill.description: Launch Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, or Copilot in a new terminal and optionally capture the agent response.
skill.summary: Launch a selected AI coding agent in a separate terminal with provider-specific options and output capture.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The skill legitimately launches coding agents, but its core path interpolates command text into shell interpreters across supported platforms. Its cookbooks also mandate disabling approvals or sandboxing, while captured output and conversation summaries can persist on disk. Documentation-only API key, Markdown, UUID, and obfuscation matches were dismissed.

remediation.issue: Provider cookbooks mandate bypassing approval and sandbox controls.
remediation.suggestion: Default to sandboxed execution with normal approvals. Require explicit, informed confirmation before enabling any unrestricted mode.

remediation.issue: Caller-controlled commands are interpolated into shell programs and executed with shell interpreters.
remediation.suggestion: Build provider commands from strict allowlists and argument arrays. Pass prompts as separate arguments and remove shell=True execution.

remediation.issue: Agent output and executable scripts use shared temporary paths without secure creation or cleanup.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private temporary directory, create files atomically with mode 0600, reject symlinks, and delete every artifact after use.

remediation.issue: Conversation summaries are written into a repository file and forwarded to another provider.
remediation.suggestion: Request explicit disclosure consent, redact credentials and private data, and pass summaries through protected temporary storage or standard input.
Track generated output paths internally and reject any path outside the private output directory before reading.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory Agent Safety Bypass
semantic_findings.description: Provider guidance requires unrestricted modes that disable command approvals and, for Codex, the sandbox. A spawned agent can therefore modify files and execute commands without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cookbooks explicitly direct automatic or bypass modes. The Codex flag is documented in the same file as skipping all confirmations and removing the sandbox.

semantic_findings.title: Conversation History Persistence and Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The summary workflow writes conversation history into a repository prompt file and sends it to a selected external agent. Sensitive context can persist or cross provider boundaries.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly requires replacing template fields with conversation history and passing that prompt to another tool. The template already contains persisted conversation summaries.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Local File Read
semantic_findings.description: read_fork_output accepts any path and reads it without verifying that fork_terminal created it. A caller can use the helper to read arbitrary files accessible to the process.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: For an existing path outside the expected naming pattern, the derived done path remains unchanged and the function immediately opens the supplied path.

content.user_title: Spawn Coding Agents in New Terminals
content.value_statement: Launching different coding agents requires provider-specific commands and output handling. This skill selects a supported CLI, opens a terminal, and optionally captures its response.
actual_capabilities: Selects Claude Code by default or uses a requested supported agent.
Supports Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot command patterns.
Opens agent sessions on macOS, Windows, WSL, and Linux.
Chooses documented model and interactive options for each provider.
Captures provider-formatted agent responses or full terminal debug output in temporary files.
Detects common authentication failures and can open provider login sessions.
limitations: Each provider CLI must already be installed and available on the system path.
Authentication and supported models depend on the selected provider account.
Windows capture cannot block until completion in every terminal path.
Provider guidance can disable safety controls, and captured output can remain in shared temporary files.

use_cases.title: Open a Focused Coding Session
use_cases.description: Launch the preferred coding agent in a separate terminal for an isolated repository task.

use_cases.title: Compare Provider Results
use_cases.description: Run the same review request with different agent CLIs and inspect their captured responses.

use_cases.title: Hand Off Active Context
use_cases.description: Start another agent with a concise conversation summary and a clearly defined next request.

prompt_templates.title: Open the Default Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn the default coding agent in a new terminal for the current repository.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup without a task prompt

prompt_templates.title: Assign a Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Codex in a new terminal to review the current changes for defects and missing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Second Opinion
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Gemini to analyze the failing tests. Capture the clean response so I can compare its diagnosis here.

prompt_templates.title: Transfer Project Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Cursor with a redacted summary of this conversation. Ask it to inspect the architecture and propose a migration sequence.

output_examples.input: Spawn the default agent for this repository.
output_examples.output: Opened a Claude Code session in a new terminal for the current working directory.

output_examples.input: Use Codex to review the tests and capture its response.
output_examples.output: Started a Codex review session. The captured response is available from the generated temporary output path.
Opened a Gemini login session and waited for the authentication flow to finish.

best_practices: Verify that the selected CLI is installed and authenticated before spawning it.
Keep sandboxing and approvals enabled unless the repository and prompt are fully trusted.
Redact secrets before context handoff and remove captured output files after use.
anti_patterns: Do not place untrusted prompt text directly inside a shell command.
Do not disable approvals or sandboxing for unknown repositories.
Do not persist credentials, private conversations, or sensitive agent output in shared temporary files.

faq.question: Which agent starts when I do not name one?
faq.answer: Claude Code is the configured default agent.

faq.question: Which coding agents are supported?
faq.answer: The cookbooks cover Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot.

faq.question: Does the skill install provider CLIs?
faq.answer: No. Each CLI must already be installed and available on the system path.

faq.question: Can it capture an agent response?
faq.answer: Yes. It can save clean agent output or complete debug output and return the file path.

faq.question: Does it support every operating system?
faq.answer: It has branches for macOS, Windows, WSL, and Linux, but terminal behavior varies by environment.

faq.question: What security precautions are required?
faq.answer: Use sandboxed modes, review commands, avoid untrusted prompts, redact secrets, and delete temporary output after use.
